acceptance_criteria.criterion: POST /api/projects/:slug/archive transitions COMPLETE to ARCHIVED in both .meta.json and project-ledger.json
POST /api/projects/:slug/unarchive transitions ARCHIVED back to COMPLETE
Both archive and unarchive update last_updated
All operations performed under project lock with atomic writes
Unit tests for all happy paths and error cases pass

summary: Added withLock import from ../src/storage/file-lock.js to gui/api.ts.
Implemented handleArchiveProject: validates COMPLETE status, acquires project lock, updates root index status to ARCHIVED (which auto-syncs .meta.json), returns {archived: true, slug}.
Implemented handleUnarchiveProject: validates ARCHIVED status, acquires project lock, updates root index status to COMPLETE (which auto-syncs .meta.json), returns {unarchived: true, slug}.
Updated handleDeleteProject guard from `!== 'COMPLETE'` to `!['COMPLETE', 'ARCHIVED'].includes(...)` so archived projects can be deleted.
Added POST /api/projects/:slug/archive and POST /api/projects/:slug/unarchive routes to matchRoute() in server.ts.
Added 10 new tests in tests/gui/api.test.ts: 5 for handleArchiveProject, 4 for handleUnarchiveProject, 1 for delete-archived.
All 37 test files, 1145 tests pass — zero regressions.

comments.note: handleArchiveProject and handleUnarchiveProject use withLock(store.storageDir, ...) + store.writeRootIndex() inside the lock. writeRootIndex auto-syncs .meta.json, which means both files are updated atomically within one lock scope — consistent with the existing updateWorkPackageWithSync pattern.

The POST /api/projects/:slug/archive and /unarchive routes are added to matchRoute() rather than the special POST block, since they require no body parsing. This is consistent with other body-less routes (DELETE).

summary: All 8 acceptance criteria verified against source code and test suite.
AC-1: handleArchiveProject writes ARCHIVED to root index via writeRootIndex, which auto-syncs .meta.json inside withLock scope — both files updated atomically. Test verifies both.
AC-2: Status guard `meta!.status !== 'COMPLETE'` → validationError (VALIDATION_ERROR → HTTP 400). Tests cover IN_PROGRESS and already-ARCHIVED cases.
AC-3: handleUnarchiveProject writes COMPLETE to root index via writeRootIndex auto-sync inside withLock. Test verifies both files.
AC-4: Status guard `meta!.status !== 'ARCHIVED'` → validationError. Test covers COMPLETE input.
AC-5: handleDeleteProject guard updated to `!['COMPLETE', 'ARCHIVED'].includes(meta!.status)` at api.ts:406. Dedicated test confirms ARCHIVED deletion succeeds.

AC-6: writeProjectMeta called by writeRootIndex always sets last_updated to current timestamp (ledger-store.ts:286). Timestamp tests for both handlers use a 5ms delay and >= comparison — confirmed correct.
AC-7: withLock(store.storageDir, ...) wraps writeRootIndex in both handlers, matching the atomic write pattern used throughout the codebase.
AC-8: Full test suite passes — 39 test files, 1167 tests, zero failures. Test count is 22 higher than implementation baseline (1145), consistent with WP-003 tests now included.
Routes POST /api/projects/:slug/archive and /unarchive correctly registered in matchRoute() at server.ts:250-269.

comments.note: Mild TOCTOU window: status is read from .meta.json before lock acquisition; root index is updated inside the lock without re-validating status. A race between two concurrent archive POSTs could theoretically archive an already-ARCHIVED project without returning VALIDATION_ERROR. Consistent with the pre-existing pattern in handleDeleteProject and acceptable for a single-server GUI. Note for future: consider re-reading status inside the lock for stricter guarantees.

The last_updated timestamp test uses >= comparison with a 5ms setTimeout delay. In theory the Node.js timer could collapse when the machine is under load, making timestamps equal and the test still pass. Assertion could be tightened to > in a future hardening pass, but this is a pre-existing pattern and not a regression risk.

summary: Code review PASS. Implementation is architecturally correct, consistent, and well-tested.

handleArchiveProject and handleUnarchiveProject follow the established api.ts handler pattern exactly: assertSafeSlug → ledgerDirExists check → readProjectMeta → status validation → withLock + writeRootIndex → return result.

Atomicity confirmed: writeRootIndex delegates to writeProjectMeta (ledger-store.ts:185) inside the lock, updating both project-ledger.json and .meta.json within one lock scope. Consistent with all other state-mutating handlers.
Route registration in server.ts matchRoute() is correct and unambiguous for POST /api/projects/:slug/archive and /unarchive. Both handlers are properly imported.
Delete guard update is correct: !['COMPLETE', 'ARCHIVED'].includes(meta.status) with updated error message. Semantics match the intent.
Type safety is solid: 'ARCHIVED' is a well-defined member of ProjectStatus in enums.ts; no string literals escape the type system.

Test coverage is comprehensive: happy path (both handlers verify root index + meta), last_updated advancement, VALIDATION_ERROR on wrong-status input (multiple cases), NOT_FOUND on missing project, and delete-of-archived. 1167 tests, zero failures.

Pre-existing TOCTOU pattern (status read from .meta.json outside the lock, not re-validated inside) is acceptable for a single-server GUI and consistent with handleDeleteProject and other handlers. No action needed.

comments.note: The TOCTOU window (status validated from readProjectMeta() outside the lock, not re-read inside withLock) is a pre-existing pattern also present in handleDeleteProject. For a future hardening pass, re-reading status inside the lock would close the theoretical race window for concurrent archive POSTs. No action required now.

Timestamp test assertion uses `>=` rather than `>` with a 5ms delay. Pre-existing pattern throughout the test suite. Could be hardened to `>` in a future cleanup, but carries no regression risk as-is.

New handler JSDoc blocks document behaviour, error types, and preconditions but omit @param/@returns tags. Consistent with how other handlers (e.g. handleDeleteProject, handleGetProject) are documented in the same file — no drift introduced.
